Summary: Mainframe to Salesforce Revenue Cloud Migration - Membership Renewal & Billing Communications
Description:
Retire the 10 legacy COBOL batch programs (ACSC membership renewal / billing / card-decline notification pipeline) and rebuild the equivalent business logic natively on Salesforce Revenue Cloud (CPQ + Billing + Subscription Management).

Source system inventory and legacy behavior: docs/cobol-legacy/README.md
Target architecture: docs/salesforce-design/high-level-design.md
Process flows: docs/salesforce-design/workflows.md
Apex design scaffold: force-app/main/default/classes/

Scope covers: renewal SMS/push eligibility notifications (MD021EX, MD022 family), billing email (MD134ML), card-decline/dunning email (MD572EM), and EFT reject / bill-plan reconciliation (MD058CB).

Summary: Implement Outbound Notification Delivery via MOVEit (PGP-Encrypted File Handoff)
Description:
Legacy and target both deliver SMS/Push/Email content as a file, not a live API call: generate a .txt/.csv extract, PGP-encrypt it, and deliver via MOVEit to a shared folder for the downstream sender system to pick up.

Acceptance Criteria:
- NotificationGatewayService accumulates per-channel records across a batch run and flushes one file per channel per run, instead of one callout per message
- File layout matches (or is explicitly reconciled with) each legacy program's existing flat-file record layout, since the downstream consumer is not changing
- PGP encryption responsibility is confirmed: MOVEit Automation encrypting server-side (recommended default) vs. an external pre-encryption hop - Apex has no native OpenPGP support
- Salesforce -> MOVEit transport confirmed as MOVEit's HTTPS/REST upload API via Named Credential - Apex has no native SFTP client
- Governor-limit review updated to reflect batched file uploads instead of per-message callouts

Status note: in progress - see force-app/main/default/classes/NotificationGatewayService.cls.

Summary: Build EFT Reject / Bill-Plan Reconciliation Batch (EftReconciliationBatch)
Description:
Replace MD058CB: reconcile EFT card-auto-update rejects against household bill-plan status, generating out-of-sync/out-of-territory correspondence and SMS/Push/Email notifications.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Eft_Cau_Reject__c staging object defined for inbound EFT reject records
- EftReconciliationBatch deployed, covering the bill-plan/lodge-type/days-to-expiration branches
- Explicit business decision recorded on the dormant bill-plan-flip-to-AM logic (currently disabled in production since MEM-480905) - confirm permanently retired before finalizing
- Retry/checkpoint semantics validated against actual at-least-once vs. exactly-once processing requirements (legacy program has GO TO-based deadlock retry with no direct Apex equivalent)
- Parity-tested against legacy MD058CB output for a full semi-monthly cycle

Status note: design scaffold exists (force-app/main/default/classes/EftReconciliationBatch.cls) - the largest and highest-risk program in scope (2,200+ lines of source).

Summary: Parallel Run & Validation Against Legacy Output
Description:
Run each migrated wave side by side with its legacy COBOL equivalent for at least one full billing/renewal cycle, diffing output before treating Salesforce as authoritative.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Diff process defined comparing legacy flat-file extracts to Salesforce Correspondence__c records / generated files, per wave
- Sign-off obtained per program family before cutover
- Data-quality edge cases the legacy code already handles (e.g. all-zero phone numbers, missing country codes) confirmed as carried over correctly

Switch the notification pickup to source from the Salesforce/MOVEit-delivered files, retire the corresponding JCL schedule per program, and keep each COBOL program dormant for one full cycle before removal.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Downstream file consumer repointed to the Salesforce-generated extracts with no format changes required (or format changes coordinated in advance)
- JCL schedule retired per program family only after its parallel-run sign-off
- Rollback plan documented in case a retired program needs to be reactivated during the dormancy period
